pageCache.text:
A Catholic School where
community, faith and excellence
help every child flourish.
EXCELLENCE
High expectations and high-quality teaching and care that help every pupil achieve their full potential.
INCLUSIVITY
A welcoming, supportive school where every child is known, loved and encouraged to belong.
COMMUNITY
Strong partnerships between school, parish and families, built on shared values and respect.
CREATIVITY
Opportunities to explore ideas and talents through learning that builds confidence and imagination.
We are proud to be a happy and highly successful school, living in the example of Christ’s love and committed to helping every member of our community flourish and succeed.
St Richard’s is a Catholic school where community, academic excellence, pastoral care and faith come together in a vibrant and purposeful learning environment. With dedicated staff, wonderful pupils and supportive families, we work in partnership to create positive experiences that lead to confident, successful futures.
We would love to welcome you to see our learning community in action.
Discover our school in action, meet the community and experience daily learning and care.
Find essential information, guidance and updates to support your child throughout their school journey.
Life at St Richard’s
Learn how the school day is structured, from lessons and breaktimes to enrichment and support.
OUR SCHOOL MISSION
Community
A caring, respectful environment where pupils, families and staff work together in partnership.
Knowledge
High expectations for learning, supported by excellent teaching and a curriculum that opens future opportunities.
Charity
Living Christ’s example through service, generosity and compassion for others, especially those most in need.
Faith in Action
Christ is at the centre of our daily school life. We witness His love for us through kindness, high expectations in behaviour, uniform and care for each other, as well as through parish involvement, charity work and support for those who are most vulnerable.
“I have come that all will have life and have it to the full”
Academic Excellence
Our academic standards are amongst the very best in the country. In 2025 we were placed 9th nationally in The Times’ League Tables for similar schools. We are extremely proud of the achievements of our pupils across all subjects and therefore the options that they have for their futures.
All Grades 7-9
Eng and Maths 4-9
Eng and Maths 5-9
Attainment
Grade 4 in all Subjects
Grade 5 in all Subjects
School Life Highlights
Pupils are welcomed to school each day by members of the Senior Team and clear routines, caring tutors and high standards of behaviour. This supports a calm and efficient atmosphere where learning isn’t interrupted. There are many opportunities for enrichment in addition to curriculum studies and additional support for pupils from both our SEND and Chaplaincy teams.
Community & Partnerships
We work closely with our five feeder primary schools, from Hastings to Seaford, ensuring an all-through approach to learning and faith. Our central place within the parish and wider community strengthens pupils’ sense of belonging through charity work, service and active participation in parish life, meaning that the partnership between school, parish and home is seamless and consistent.
Come and see us!
See the school in action, meet our staff and pupils, and experience daily life first-hand.
Work at St Richard’s
Learn about working in a supportive, values-led environment committed to helping young people flourish and adults fulfil their ambitions.
Our community
Discover strong partnerships with families, parishes and local organisations enrich learning, belonging and opportunities for pupils.

Careers
Preparing pupils for life beyond St Richard’s
At St Richard’s, Careers Education and Guidance prepares pupils for life beyond full-time education. It is available to all pupils and is central to our commitment to helping every pupil flourish and succeed.
Our programme supports pupils to explore their interests, recognise their strengths and make informed decisions about their future. We aim to inspire and motivate pupils while providing clear, impartial information, advice and guidance.
We believe that every pupil has the ability and potential to grow and achieve. Where barriers exist, we work closely with pupils and families to ensure that every pupil is supported to achieve their potential and move forward with confidence — whether that next step is sixth form, college, an apprenticeship or employment.
CAREERS LEAD
Careers education at St Richard’s is led by our Careers Lead, who oversees the development and delivery of the programme.
For further information about careers education, guidance or provider access, please contact:
Mrs LyonsCareers Leadmrslyonsc@strichardscc.com01323 721310
How Careers Education Develops at St Richard’s
We aim to enable all pupils to flourish – academically, socially and spiritually – growing together in friendship and in faith. Support by dedicated staff, strong pastoral care and a shared sense of purpose, our pupils leave St Richard’s well prepared for the future challenges and opportunities ahead.
By the End of Year 9
By the end of Year 9, pupils will have:
· Developed an understanding of how to make informed decisions about GCSE subject choices
· Begun to recognise their skills and strengths, such as teamwork and meeting deadlines
· Received guidance and advice from key staff, including Form Tutors, Pastoral Leaders and the Careers Lead
· Used careers websites and labour market information to explore areas of interest
· Reflected on and recorded their achievements, including progress towards target grades
· Had opportunities to meet employers through workshops and the school careers fair
· Been able to use the Careers section in the school library
This ensures pupils are well prepared to make informed choices as they move into Key Stage 4
By the End of Year 11
By the end of Year 11, pupils will have:
· A clear understanding of post-16 education, training and apprenticeship pathways
· Knowledge of a wide range of further education, training and career opportunities
· Experience researching and comparing options
· Accessed personalised careers advice and guidance
· Used careers websites to explore areas of interest
· Completed work experience
· Taken part in a mock interview with an employer
· Reflected on their skills and strengths, including teamwork and meeting deadlines
· Recorded achievements such as academic progress and leadership roles
· Developed confidence, resilience and readiness for adult life
· Regular access to the Careers section in the school library
Our aim is that every pupil leaves St Richard’s prepared to take the next step with clarity, confidence and ambition.
Personal Guidance and Equal Access
Every pupil has access to impartial careers advice.
The Careers Lead and pastoral team provide:
· One-to-one guidance interviews
· Targeted support for pupils who may face barriers to progression
· Additional guidance for pupils with SEND
· Support with applications, interviews and transition planning
We are committed to ensuring equal access to high-quality careers guidance for all pupils.
Career Share – Parents and Carers
We value the support of parents and carers in helping pupils understand the world of work.
Through the Career Share initiative, parents and carers are invited to share their experiences, career journeys and professional knowledge with pupils. This may include speaking at events, supporting workshops or contributing to careers activities.
If you would like to get involved, please contact the Careers Lead.
Careers Policies
You can find further information about careers education at St Richard’s in the documents below:
Additional statutory information is available on our Statutory Information & Policies page.
Provider Access Statement
The Impact of the Careers Programme
Careers Information & Resources
Practical guidance to support pupils and families at each stage.
Applying for College or Sixth Form
Choosing your subjects
Find out which A levels you need to get to the next step? E.g. what do you need to get onto the university course / career you want?
Do an internet search for the course requirements for you chosen course/career.
It is always worth finding out what universities generally want for their courses or for specific courses; you can find this information by searching on the UCAS website: https://www.ucas.com/
You can also look at the requirements for the Russell Group Universities: https://www.informedchoices.ac.uk/
A good suggestion is to choose 3 subjects relevant to your career or university choice and 1 subject you know you will enjoy which might not be relevant to keep your enjoyment levels up. Colleges often like you to choose 4 subjects and perhaps drop one course if you find it too hard.
Think about doing an apprenticeship at college, most colleges offer them. Please refer to the page on apprenticeships for more information.
Choosing your College
Have a look at the colleges in the local area, consider:
Do they run the courses you need to do?Can you afford to travel to the college each day?Can you get up early enough to get there?Don’t worry if your friends are not going to the college you are thinking about, you will probably make new friends anyway.Go to the open evenings / guided tour days. If you miss these, contact the college and go and see it anyway.Trying using the UCAS progress website, you can explore and compare the courses available at colleges, sixth forms and training providers across the local area. You can search by postcode, subject, and school, college or work-based learning provider for courses for 16-19 year olds.
https://www.ucasprogress.com/
Applying to a College
Talk about your college application with your parent / carer and get them to check your application for errors / spelling mistakes.
Most applications are made through the Careers East Sussex website. You will have received your username and password via email. Please ensure that you have had your application checked before you submit.
Apprenticeships
Depending on the apprenticeship offered, you can earn money while being trained on the job and get qualifications including a degree, A-levels, NVQs, etc.The apprenticeship website is huge as it is for apprentices, employers, parents, colleges and more, so here are some sections you might be interested in if you just want a quick look:
Types of apprenticeship if there are no current vacancies, remember to register and set up an email alert.Videos & Pictures videos of interviews and images in the media gallerySearch for an apprenticeship in the local area by searching for Apprenticeship / East SussexNewsletterApprenticeships on Twitter Follow @ApprenticeshipsApprenticeships on Sussex website
https://www.findapprenticeship.service.gov.uk/apprenticeshipsearch
http://www.apprenticeships-in-sussex.com/
Labour Market Information
Labour Market Information Bulletin
RISKY BUSINESS: WHAT ARE THE UK RISKIEST JOBS?
Labour Market Information (LMI)
Employablity
What is employability?Employability skills are defined as:
A set of attributes, skills and knowledge that all labour market participants should possess to ensure they have the capability of being effective in the workplace to the benefit of themselves, their employer, and the wider economy.
Academic skills: includes specialist knowledge, ability to apply knowledge, logical thinking, critical analysis, and problem-solving, written and spoken communication, ability to use numerical data, computer literacy and research skills.
Personal Development Skills: includes self-confidence, self-discipline, self-reliance, awareness of strengths and weaknesses, creativity, independence, knowledge of international affairs, desire to go on learning, ability to reflect, reliability, integrity, honesty and regard for others.
Enterprise or business skills: includes entrepreneurial skills, ability to prioritise tasks, time management, interpersonal skills, presentational skills, ability to work in teams and leadership skills, commercial awareness, flexibility, innovation, independence and risk-taking.
So what does employability mean for you?
Employability is about much more than just getting your first job it’s about having a positive self-image and presenting yourself successfully, both as you leave school and throughout your life.
Your skills, knowledge and personal attributes and the ability to convey them effectively all contribute to your employability as do your personal circumstances and labour market conditions.
You probably already know that you need to get good results, complete some work experience and improve your skills in order to get a good job. As part of this process you will take part in a mock interview in Year 10.
Work Experience
Year 10 pupils have one week block placement in the summer term. This week is particular valuable as it really gives the pupils a chance to experience the world of work. The week should not necessarily be thought of as a ‘Career Taster’ week, as there are some organisations that will not take pupils under the age of 16.
All placements are organised via the Careers East Sussex database and pupils will have usernames and passwords issued to them.
https://www.careerseastsussex.co.uk/login
Qualifications Framework
Click here for the “Do you know your levels” sheet
Volunteering
Volunteering is simple. It is about giving your time to do something useful, without getting paid. It is a useful way of getting experience which is so valuable when applying for jobs. It can also be a great way to: meet new people, learn new skills and gain useful experience.
The range of opportunities is huge and there is no age limit. Whatever skills and experience you have, there is something that you can do.
Once you start volunteering you should usually expect:
If you are not clear about anything, do not be afraid to ask someone.
Hints to help you start volunteering:
Think about what you want from volunteering: new skills, fun, a chance to contribute to a cause?Think about what you have to offer: enthusiasm, work skills, life skills?Work out roughly how much time you have to give, and how many times a week or month.Remember that anyone can volunteer: whatever your skills, experience or background you should be able to find an opportunity.Ask questions: do not be shy about asking questions as you go through the process of applying for an opportunity.Just try it: often the most difficult part of volunteering is making the first move, so be brave!

Behaviour System
Encouraging positive behaviour and supporting growth
At St Richard’s, we are committed to developing the whole child. Our Behaviour System is designed to reinforce the positive attitudes and actions that help our community flourish.
We believe in recognising success, encouraging responsibility and responding to mistakes with fairness, consistency and dignity.
Recognising and Rewarding Positive Behaviour
Positive behaviour is celebrated in many ways across the school.
House points are awarded for achievement, attendance, hard work, participation and kindness. Pupils may also receive:
We believe that encouragement and recognition build confidence and strengthen the values that shape our community.
Verbal praise
Positions of responsibility
Representative honours and prefect status
Reward stickers and postcards home
Early lunch passes
The Crest Award
The Crest celebrates each pupil’s wider development during their five years at St Richard’s.
To achieve The Crest, pupils take part in a range of activities, including:
Parents and carers receive an annual update on their child’s progress towards The Crest. Pupils who complete the full award are recognised at special celebration events, with families invited to share in this achievement.
Leadership opportunities
Enrichment in sport or the Arts
Charity work
Peer support
Work-related learning
When Mistakes Happen
When mistakes are made, we work alongside pupils, parents and carers to reflect, learn and move forward in the spirit of reconciliation.
Consequences are applied fairly and proportionately, taking into account the nature of the incident and the individual circumstances involved. A range of responses may be used, including:
Parents and carers are asked to monitor behaviour points online and support constructive conversations at home. If a pupil is placed in after-school detention, parents will be notified by email at least 24 hours in advance, with clear information about the reason.
For more serious breaches of school expectations, Saturday detentions may be issued. In cases of serious misconduct, a suspension may be necessary. Permanent exclusion is extremely rare and would only be considered where required to safeguard the wellbeing of the wider school community.
Withdrawal of certain privileges
Subject or behaviour reports
After-school detentions
A Fair and Consistent Approach
Clear expectations, consistent responses and open communication help pupils feel secure and supported. When we work together with families, we create the stability that allows young people to thrive.
Full procedural details can be found in our Pastoral Care & Behaviour Management Policy on the Statutory Information page.

Community Expectations
Living our values everyday
At St Richard’s Catholic College, we are proud to be a school community built on kindness, respect and a shared commitment to helping one another flourish.
Our Community Expectations reflect the way we choose to live and learn together. Rooted in our Catholic values of Community, Knowledge and Charity, they help to create a calm, safe and purposeful environment where every pupil feels valued and supported.
These expectations are not simply rules; they are shared commitments that guide daily life at St Richard’s and ensure that our school remains a place of dignity, belonging and high standards for all.
Further Information
Positive Behaviour and Relationships
Strong relationships are at the heart of life at St Richard’s. We want every pupil to feel respected, valued and safe.
Expectations apply both within school and beyond the school gates where behaviour affects the safety, wellbeing or reputation of our community.
We are clear that bullying, discrimination or unkind behaviour are not acceptable. When concerns are raised, they are always taken seriously and handled with care, fairness and consistency.
If a pupil experiences or witnesses behaviour that causes concern, they should speak to a trusted adult — such as their Form Tutor, Pastoral Leader or any member of staff. Parents and carers are also encouraged to contact us directly so we can work together to resolve concerns.
Pupils can also report concerns confidentially through Whisper, our online reporting system.
Wearing the correct uniform and presenting themselves smartly are also part of our shared expectations, reflecting pride in belonging to St Richard’s. Full guidance can be found on our Uniform page.
For full details on positive behaviour, please see our Pastoral Care & Behaviour Management Policy and Anti-Bullying Policy on the Statutory Information page.

Pupil Wellbeing & Parent and Carer Support
Supporting every pupil to feel safe, happy and able to flourish
At St Richard’s, we believe that pupils thrive when they feel safe, supported and valued.
When you send your child to us, you are placing your trust in our care. We take this responsibility seriously. Our aim is to ensure that every pupil feels confident, included and ready to learn, so they can grow both academically and personally.
We work closely with parents and carers because we know that strong partnerships between home and school help young people succeed.
Pastoral Care at St Richard’s
Every pupil is supported by a dedicated pastoral team throughout their time at the college.
Together, this team ensures that every pupil is guided, supported and encouraged to succeed.
Support for Pupils and Families
We encourage parents and carers to contact us whenever they have a concern – no matter how small.
You might contact us about:

Pupil Absence
What to do if your child is absent, and how to request time away from school
Report an Absence
If your child is unwell or unable to attend school, please contact us as soon as possible on the first day of absence.
If your child is absent for more than one day, please keep the school informed.
Telephone: 01424 731070
Contact the school office by telephone
Provide your child’s name and form
Give the reason for the absence
Request Time Away from School
The information below explains how to request planned absence during term time.
There is no automatic right to take your child out of school during term time.
The Department for Education guidance means that a headteacher can only approve absence in exceptional circumstances. It is the headteacher’s decision whether an absence can be authorised, and how many days may be approved.
If you believe your request meets these criteria, please complete the Withdrawal from Learning Application form at the bottom of the page. A response will be sent to you as soon as possible.
If the absence requested is not considered to be an exceptional circumstance and you take your child out of school, the absence will be recorded as unauthorised in line with County Council guidance.
Unauthorised Absence and Penalty Notices
If an absence is unauthorised, the Education Support, Behaviour and Attendance Service will be notified and a Penalty Notice will be issued.
Penalty Notices are issued to each parent for each child taken out of school.
Form to Request Time Away from School
All absence requests during term time must be completed using the Withdrawal from Learning Application form. Letters will not be accepted.
The form should be returned to the school at least 14 days before the start of the absence.
Need to get in touch?
If you need to report an absence or have any questions, our team is here to help.

pageCache.pageTitle: Adverse Weather Information | St Richard’s Catholic College, Bexhill
pageCache.text:
Adverse Weather
Guidance on what to do and where to check during severe weather
We will always make every effort to keep St Richard’s open. However, in severe weather, the safety of our pupils and staff is our priority. A decision to close, delay opening, or close early will always be based on a careful health and safety risk assessment.
Checking if St Richard’s is Open
The most up-to-date information will always be published on our website, appearing as a banner on the homepage. This will include a clear message confirming whether or not St Richard’s is open or closed.
Where possible, a clear decision about whether the college is open or closed will be shared by 6.45am. In some cases, this may be slightly later, as we need to confirm local conditions and public transport availability before making a final decision.
Need to get in touch?
If you cannot find the information you need, our team is here to help. We aim to respond as quickly as possible and will always do our best to support you.
Other Ways to Get Updates
Please listen for updates on local radio stations: Radio Sussex, Heart, and Arrow FM.
Contacting St Richard’s
If you still need to contact the college, staff will usually be available to take calls from 7.00am.
We understand that unexpected closures can be disruptive, and we appreciate your patience and support when decisions need to be made quickly in changing conditions.

pageCache.text:
Free School Meals
Making sure every pupil can enjoy a healthy meal at school
We know that access to a healthy meal is an important part of a pupil’s ability to learn, grow and feel well.
Free School Meals provide practical support for families and help ensure that pupils can access a healthy meal each day in a way that is discreet, inclusive and part of everyday school life.
If you think your child may be eligible, we encourage you to apply.
Who is Eligible for Free School Meals?
Your child may be eligible for Free School Meals if you receive certain benefits.
Eligibility depends on both the benefits you receive and your household income.
Even if your child does not wish to take a free school meal, we still encourage you to apply if you are eligible. This is because eligibility also allows the school to receive additional funding – the Pupil Premium – which helps us provide further support for pupils.
If you are not sure whether you are eligible, you can check online or contact us for help.
Universal Credit
Income Support
Jobseeker’s Allowance
Employment and Support Allowance
Child Tax Credit (subject to income thresholds)
How to Apply
Applications for Free School Meals are made through East Sussex County Council.
Once your application has been approved, the school will be notified and support will be put in place.
If you need help with your application, please contact the school office and we will be happy to assist you.
Support at St Richard’s
At St Richard’s, we ensure that support is provided in a discreet and respectful way.
Pupils receiving Free School Meals are able to:
Access school meals as part of the normal lunch system
Take part fully in school activities
Receive additional support where appropriate
Our aim is to ensure that all pupils feel included and supported, regardless of their circumstances.
Pupil Premium
If your child is eligible for Free School Meals, the school may also receive additional funding known as Pupil Premium.
This funding is provided by the government to support pupils and help them achieve their full potential.
At St Richard’s, Pupil Premium funding is used to:
provide additional academic support
support wellbeing and inclusion
help pupils access opportunities across school life

pageCache.pageTitle: Prayer & Worship | St Richard’s Catholic College
pageCache.text:
Prayer & Worship
Daily prayer at the heart of school life
At St Richard’s, prayer and liturgy are central to who we are as a Catholic community. Our faith shapes the rhythm of each day and brings us together in reflection, gratitude and celebration.
Daily Prayer
Every day, pupils and staff take part in collective prayer. Prayer takes place during registration, before lunch and at the end of the school day.
Daily prayer is supported by digital resources prepared by our Lay Chaplain, and pupils areencouraged to take an active role in leading and developing this time of reflection.
Each Friday morning, pupils gather in the Chapel before school for Morning Prayer of theChurch.
“I love the part that prayer plays every day.”
Assemblies and Reflection
Assemblies are rooted in Catholic teaching and take place weekly for each year group, withadditional Upper and Lower School assemblies throughout the term.
Every form prepares and leads an assembly during the year. This helps pupils to grow inconfidence and leadership, and to reflect more deeply on faith and values.
Mass and the Liturgical Year
The Holy Sacrifice of the Mass is celebrated at the beginning of each term and on High andHoly Days.
Each form also takes part in a Mass or Celebration of the Word in the Chapel during the year. Our annual Advent Service and Mass of Thanksgiving for Grandparents are important moments in the College’s liturgical calendar and are open to the wider community.
Music plays an important part in our liturgies, with pupils actively involved in singing andplaying instruments.
The Sacraments and the Chapel
Pupils have the opportunity to receive the Sacrament of Reconciliation during Advent andLent, with the sacrament also available on request throughout the year.
The Chapel is open during break and lunchtime, offering a quiet space for prayer andreflection. Pupils may also take part in Adoration of the Blessed Sacrament each week.
“The chapel is a fabulous and well used focal point for prayer and liturgy at the school.”
Through these opportunities, we support pupils in developing a mature spiritual life and an active participation in the life of the Church.
Prayer and worship are closely connected with the learning pupils experience in Religious Education and the work of the chaplaincy team.
For full details, please refer to our Prayer & Liturgy Policy in the Statutory Information & Policies section of this website.

pageCache.pageTitle: Religious Education | St Richard’s Catholic College
pageCache.text:
Religious Education
Learning about faith, belief and the world
Religious Education is a core subject at St Richard’s Catholic College and plays a central role in the life of the school. Through Religious Education, pupils develop knowledge and understanding of the Catholic faith while also exploring wider questions about belief, morality and the world around them.
Our curriculum encourages pupils to think deeply, ask questions and engage respectfully with different viewpoints. As pupils progress through the school, their knowledge and understanding grows in depth and complexity, helping them to develop both academically and personally.
Pupils study Religious Education throughout their time at St Richard’s, with three lessons each week and regular homework to support their learning.
A Curriculum Built on Strong Foundations
The Religious Education curriculum at St Richard’s is carefully structured so that knowledge builds over time, beginning in Year 7 and developing through each stage of a pupil’s education.
At Key Stage 3, the curriculum follows the Religious Education Directory (2023). This programme presents the Catholic faith through the narrative of the Christian story, often described as the history of salvation. Pupils learn about scripture, belief, tradition and the teachings of the Church, helping them understand the foundations of Catholic faith and practice.
This approach allows pupils to revisit important ideas as they progress through the curriculum, deepening their understanding each year.
Key Stage 4: GCSE Religious Studies
At Key Stage 4, pupils study GCSE Religious Studies (Edexcel).
The course builds on the knowledge developed in Key Stage 3 and explores Catholic beliefs and practices in greater depth. Pupils study key aspects of Catholic life, including sources of authority, forms of expression and the role of faith in the modern world.
As part of the GCSE course, pupils also complete a Philosophy and Ethics module, where they explore philosophical arguments for the existence of God and examine moral questions in the light of the Catholic tradition.
Pupils also study the beliefs and practices of Islam, helping them develop understanding and respect for other faith traditions and the diverse world in which they live.
Developing Thoughtful and Reflective Learners
Religious Education at St Richard’s encourages pupils to think critically, discuss ideas and reflect on important questions about life and belief.
Through discussion, debate and written work, pupils learn to consider different perspectives, develop reasoned arguments and express their ideas clearly. These skills support pupils not only in Religious Education but across the wider curriculum.
By studying religion in depth, pupils develop a deeper understanding of faith, ethics and human experience, helping them grow as thoughtful and responsible members of society.
Religious Education is closely connected with the wider Catholic life of the school, including prayer and worship, chaplaincy activities and opportunities for service through Catholic Social Teaching.

pageCache.pageTitle: Reporting & Assessment | St Richard’s Catholic College
pageCache.text:
Reporting and Assessments
Clear information, shared goals, continued progress
At St Richard’s, assessment and reporting are part of how we help every pupil grow and succeed. We use assessments to guide learning, celebrate achievement and share meaningful information with pupils and their families. Our approach is designed to be clear and supportive so that parents and carers understand how pupils are progressing and what to focus on next.
Targets and progress measures
Each pupil receives an aspirational target grade based on prior attainment, including Key Stage 2 assessments and other relevant information. These targets are set using the new GCSE 9–1 scale (with 9 being the highest). Targets are reviewed regularly to reflect pupils’ progress throughout their time with us.
To support learning, teachers record “working at” scores (which show current progress), several times during the year. These help pupils and parents see how pupils are progressing in relation to their target.
Early in the year (Terms 1 and 2) pupils are expected to be working slightly below target
Mid-year (Terms 3 and 4) pupils make progress towards their target
By the end of the year (Term 6), pupils are expected to be meeting their target in end-of-year assessments and exams
Supporting progress and achievement
If a pupil’s progress falls below expectations, we identify this early and agree supportive actions. An intervention code is assigned to show where additional support is needed, which might include:
We keep families informed about these discussions and next steps through written updates and direct communication.
When pupils are performing above expectation across a number of subjects, we celebrate their achievement with a Certificate of Commendation, presented in assembly.
If a pupil is below expectation in several subjects, this may be discussed with the Pastoral Leader and appropriate support — such as report monitoring or study sessions — put in place.
After-school support sessions
Targeted revision tasks
Further assessments and feedback
What this means for pupils and parents
We want reporting at St Richard’s to support learning and strengthen partnership with families. Your child’s assessment information is shared in ways that help you see:
We design our reporting so that it is clear, helpful and focused on next steps — not just numbers or grades.
What your child has achieved
How they are progressing towards their targets
Where they are doing well
Where they may benefit from extra support
Further information
If you would like more detail about our reporting processes, please contact the School Office, who can direct you to the appropriate staff member.
Further information about assessment and reporting can also be found on our Statutory Information & Policies page.
